slides.title: Good Neighbours and Jobs
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 2: Good Neighbours and Jobs. In this unit you meet the people who live and work in your neighbourhood, and you find out what their jobs are. You learn twenty-one words for helpers, for their special clothes and equipment, and for the actions they do, from the window cleaner and the bus driver to the firefighter, the nurse and the farmer. You learn to ask questions with What and Who, to count people and objects, and to say what somebody is doing right now with is or are and a verb ending in -ing. By the end you can describe a job, name the equipment that keeps a worker safe, and be a good neighbour like the children in this unit's story, The Helpers of Warta Street. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name the different people who live and work in your neighbourhood.
Describe a job and explain what the person does in it.
Ask and answer questions using What and Who.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name the different people who live and work in your neighbourhood. You will also describe a job and explain what the person does in it. You will also ask and answer questions using What and Who. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: day, stay, tray, key, need, farmer. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Firefighters and Their Equipment and A Poem: “My Neighbourhood”. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: What and Who: Choosing the Question Word
bullets: We use question words to ask for information. What asks about a thing, an action or a job. Who asks about a person. These two little words help you find...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is What and Who: Choosing the Question Word. We use question words to ask for information. What asks about a thing, an action or a job. Who asks about a person. These two little words help you find out about the helpers in your neighbourhood. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1 — Three Sentences About a Job
Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Describe a Job. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
